_about: Surf and kite spots for the Surf / Kite modes. lat/lon sit a little offshore so the wave model has a sea grid cell. facing = rough compass direction (degrees) the beach looks out to the water: swell and onshore wind come FROM this direction, offshore wind from the opposite side. Facing values are approximate, good enough for onshore/offshore calls, not for precise peak selection. water: sea or lake (lakes have no wave or water-temperature data). Edit freely.

surf.name: Varazze
surf.notes: Liguria's best-known wave, closest real sea surf to Salzburg. Needs a S–SW (Libeccio) storm swell, best autumn to spring. Reef and beach breaks, crowded when it's on.

surf.name: Levanto
surf.notes: Sandy beach break near Cinque Terre, picks up SW swell. Friendly for learners on small days.

surf.name: Capo Mannu, Sardinia
surf.notes: The Mediterranean's most consistent surf zone, catches NW Mistral swell. Mostly reef breaks, better for intermediate+.

surf.name: Premantura / Kamenjak
surf.notes: Southern tip of Istria. Only works in strong southerly Jugo storms, rare but close (about 5 h).

surf.name: Senigallia
surf.notes: Adriatic beach break, wakes up with NE (Bora) swell in winter. Short-period waves, usually onshore.

surf.name: Scheveningen
surf.notes: Dutch surf hub by the pier. North Sea wind swell, needs light winds to be clean. Good surf schools.

surf.name: Sylt – Westerland
surf.notes: Germany's surf island. Beach breaks with sandbanks, cold water most of the year.

surf.name: Klitmøller (Cold Hawaii)
surf.notes: Reef breaks on Denmark's north-west coast. Powerful in autumn storms, intermediate+.

surf.name: Hossegor
surf.notes: World-class Atlantic beach breaks. Heavy and fast when big; beginners stay on small days and near the lifeguards.

surf.name: Biarritz – Côte des Basques
surf.notes: Mellow longboard wave at mid to low tide, classic learner spot.

surf.name: Ericeira
surf.notes: World Surfing Reserve with many reefs and points. Beginners: Foz do Lizandro beach just south.

surf.name: Peniche – Supertubos
surf.notes: Peniche peninsula faces two ways, so something usually works. Supertubos is a heavy barrel when big; Baleal side for learning.

kite.name: Podersdorf – Neusiedler See
kite.notes: Austria's main kite spot. Shallow, standing-depth water, great for learning. Best in NW wind. Ride only in the marked kite zone.

kite.name: Campione del Garda
kite.notes: Lake Garda's main kite zone. Pelèr (N) in the morning, Ora (S) from midday. Deep water, boat launches via local schools.

kite.name: Navene / Malcesine
kite.notes: East shore of Garda, catches the same thermal winds. Kiting only in designated areas and times.

kite.name: Reschensee (Lago di Resia)
kite.notes: High-alpine lake with a reliable afternoon thermal in summer. Cold water, frozen in winter (snowkiting then).

kite.name: Silvaplana
kite.notes: Engadin classic with the Maloja wind on summer afternoons. Cold water, thick wetsuit even in July.

kite.name: Lignano Sabbiadoro
kite.notes: Closest sea spot, about 3.5 h. Works with Scirocco (SE). Bora (NE) blows offshore here: dangerous.

kite.name: Nin – Kraljičina plaža
kite.notes: Shallow sandy lagoon, very beginner-friendly. Maestral (NW) in summer, Bora in winter for experts only.

kite.name: Viganj – Pelješac
kite.notes: Croatia's kite capital. Summer Maestral blows along the channel almost every afternoon.

kite.name: St. Peter-Ording
kite.notes: Huge North Sea beach, strong tides. Steady wind, lots of space, big schools.

kite.name: Tarifa – Los Lances
kite.notes: Europe's wind capital. Levante (E) is gusty and side-offshore, Poniente (W) steadier and side-on.
